prompt: Many manufactured food and drink products contain high levels of sugar, which causes many health problems. Sugary products should be made more expensive to encourage people to consume less sugar. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Currently, high consumption of sugar in processed food and drinks is related to many diseases. One potential solution is suggested, which is increasing the price of products that contain sugar in order to reduce sugar consumption. I strongly disagree with this perspective because the budget growth could induce other issues, rather than the excessive sugar intake.

On the one hand, fast food with high sugar is easier to access not only because of the low price, but also due to the large proportion of grain. If the price rockets to a sky-high level, those people could not afford this cheap energy source would look for other alternative products, which might cause other bigger problems. For example, if there are no cheap carbohydrates on the plate, folks who are undernourished would do criminals for food because other energy sources would be more expensive than carbohydrates. Therefore, it could cause social problems due to the rise in food prices.

On the other hand, however, if the expenditure on sugary foods is reduced to some extent, the price of other high-quality foods, such as proteins or seafood, would be reduced as well. This is because the food animals are fed by grains, and cheap grains could make the meat cheaper. For instance, chicken breast has been the most favourite protein source for people who are doing fitness in North America. In addition, it is also one of the most affordable meats due to the cheap grain offered by the advanced agricultural system.

In conclusion. It is too ideal to rise expense of highly processed foods that contain sugars in order to reduce public sugar consumption. I strongly disagree with this advice, and I believe it needs multiple alterations to meet the end of our purpose for promoting public health.
